extra.message: applyLedgerSort builds ORDER BY with the raw sortBy query string: qb.orderBy(`p.${sortBy}`, direction). sortBy comes straight from req.query on GET /api/payments (no allowlist, unlike leases' LEASE_SORT_COLUMNS whitelist), allowing SQL injection via a crafted ORDER BY expression such as a subquery or stacked expression. Any authenticated user (including tenants) can reach it.

runUnitWatchlist splices the stored rule value directly into a raw SQL string literal: `... AND u.${field} = '${value}'` while runTicketWatchlist correctly uses a $2 parameter. The value is supplied by staff via PUT /api/dashboard/watchlist/units and later executed unparameterized (second-order SQL injection) whenever the watchlist widget is loaded for a building.

renderRentRollExport builds a shell command with an unvalidated query parameter: `soffice --headless --convert-to ${outputFormat} ...` executed via spawn(cmd, { shell: true }). format is taken directly from req.query with no allowlist, so a staff user can inject arbitrary shell metacharacters (e.g. format=xlsx; curl ...) achieving OS command injection. (renderInspectionsExport is the safe twin: allowlist + shell:false.)

computeCustomProrationSplit constructs and executes arbitrary JavaScript from staff-controlled form input: new Function('unit','totalAmount', `return (${fields.formula});`). The formula field is taken from a multipart upload without any allowlist (computeStandardProrationSplit is the safe twin using pre-approved clauses). A staff user can supply a formula that escapes to execute arbitrary code on the server (RCE).

previewVendorInvoiceDocument performs a server-side fetch of a fully attacker-chosen documentUrl from the request body with no host/allowlist validation, enabling SSRF to internal services (cloud metadata, internal admin panels). previewVerifiedVendorInvoiceDocument is the safe twin that restricts to ALLOWED_VENDOR_DOC_HOSTS.

GET /api/properties/:propertyId/rate-benchmark fetches an arbitrary server-supplied feedUrl from the query string with fetch(feedUrl) and returns parsed contents. No URL scheme/host validation lets a staff user probe internal hosts, and combined with the XML parser in marketFeed the response body can disclose local files (see XXE finding).
GET /api/properties/:propertyId/vendor-catalog performs an unvalidated server-side fetch(feedUrl) from the query string, enabling SSRF against internal network resources.

loadRateBenchmarkFeed (used by the rate-benchmark endpoint) parses DOCTYPE/ENTITY declarations from attacker-influenced feed XML and, for SYSTEM entities, reads the referenced local file with fs.readFileSync and substitutes its contents into the response records (e.g. <!ENTITY x SYSTEM "file:///etc/passwd">). This is an XXE-style local file disclosure. loadVendorCatalogFeed is the safe twin that rejects any feed containing a DOCTYPE.

readBuildingFloorPlanSheet joins the raw sheetName route parameter onto the building folder: path.join(FLOORPLAN_DIR, buildingId) then path.join(buildingDir, sheetName). sheetName is not reduced to a bare filename (readBuildingFloorPlanSheetVerified is the safe twin using path.basename), so GET /api/properties/buildings/:buildingId/floor-plans/<sheet> with sheetName = ../../../../etc/passwd reads arbitrary server files, whose contents are returned to the caller.

storeListingAsset writes an uploaded file using the client-supplied filename directly: const displayName = part.filename ...; path.join(PUBLIC_ASSET_DIR, displayName). No MIME allowlist or size cap, and a filename containing ../ (or an absolute path) lets a staff user write files outside the intended public/listing-photos directory (arbitrary file/directory write). storeAmenityAsset is the safe twin that validates MIME, caps size, and uses a server-generated random name.

saveScreeningDecisionLetter writes the vendor-provided file name straight into the path: path.join(DECISION_LETTER_DIR, suggestedName) + fs.writeFileSync. suggestedName comes from the client-controlled x-decision-filename header in POST /api/leases/waitlist/decision-letter. A name like ../../../app/... allows arbitrary file writes on the server. saveVerifiedScreeningDecisionLetter is the safe twin that applies path.basename.

renderNoticeLetter joins the caller-supplied template name onto the templates directory without confining the result: path.join(TEMPLATES_DIR, templateName); fs.readFileSync(...). generateLeaseRenewalLetter passes the unvalidated ?template= query value here, so a manager can read arbitrary server files (path traversal). renderNoticeLetterScoped is the safe twin that verifies the resolved path stays under the templates directory.

resolveVendorCostScope only decodes the supplied JWT (app.jwt.decode) without verifying its signature, trusting attacker-supplied claims. The vendor.csv report endpoint accepts this token in the x-cost-scope header, so any authenticated user can forge a self-signed token with an arbitrary buildingId and read another building's maintenance ticket list. resolveContractorCostScope is the safe twin that calls app.jwt.verify.

cwe: CWE-345: Insufficient Verification of Data Authenticity

extra.message: viewSharedLeaseSummary trusts a query-string claim: any authenticated user can request /api/leases/:id/household-view?viewAccess=shared for ANY lease id and receive its summary (unit, dates, rent). The sharing grant is never read back off the record or matched to the caller. viewVerifiedSharedLeaseSummary is the safe twin that compares lease.tenantId/sharedWithUserId to req.authUser.id.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: submitLeaseRenewalRequest applies the whole request body to the lease entity via Object.assign(lease, req.body). A tenant submitting a renewal on their own lease can overwrite arbitrary fields — rentAmount, depositAmount, endDate, internalNotes, even transferCode/autopayBankAccount — because there is no field allowlist (updateLeaseNotes is the safe twin that copies only internalNotes).

editTicketComment updates any comment by id: comments.update({ id: commentId, ticketId: id }, { body }) after only checking the caller can view the ticket — never that the caller authored the comment. A worker assigned to a ticket can rewrite other staff's (including managers') comments and internal notes. editOwnTicketComment is the safe twin enforcing comment.authorId === req.authUser.id.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: applyRushOrderClearance makes an authorization/supplier-clearance decision purely from client-controlled request headers: `const cleared = supplierTier == 'preferred' || clearanceFlag;`. Any non-empty x-rush-clearance value (or a loose == match on x-supplier-tier) is treated as supplier approval, letting any staff member escalate a ticket to URGENT without a genuine supplier callback. applyRushOrderClearanceReviewed is the safe twin that requires clearanceFlag === 'true' and a strict tier comparison.

finalizeWaitlistOffer trusts the vendor decision with a truthiness/loose-equality check: `const staffOverride = req.authUser.role == Role.ADMIN; if (staffOverride || decision.access)`. The screening vendor returns the string 'false' for a denial, and any non-empty string is truthy — so a manager (non-admin) gets approval even when the vendor denied the applicant. finalizeWaitlistOfferReviewed is the safe twin requiring decision.access === true and strict role equality.

completePartnerApplicationHandoff redirects straight to the client-supplied x-return-url header (reply.redirect(returnTo)) with no validation of scheme or host. An API-key holder can craft links that redirect end users to arbitrary (phishing) destinations. completePartnerTourHandoff is the safe twin that only redirects when the parsed origin is in WIDGET_PARTNER_ORIGINS.

GET /api/dashboard/embed/portfolio-summary has no role restriction (only the blanket authenticate hook) and portfolioSummary() scopes by unit only for MANAGERs — for a TENANT caller scopeUnitIds stays null, so a tenant receives portfolio-wide aggregate metrics (open ticket counts and occupancy across ALL units/properties). The endpoint also strips X-Frame-Options entirely for admins (the /scoped twin instead sets a CSP frame-ancestors allowlist), allowing the admin dashboard tile to be framed by any origin.

POST /api/auth/forgot-password returns the freshly generated password-reset token to the caller in the response body ({ ok: true, devToken }) whenever the target email corresponds to an active account, with no NODE_ENV guard. Because the endpoint is public and unauthenticated, an attacker can request a reset for a victim's email and receive the token directly, enabling full account takeover. The devToken also doubles as an account-enumeration oracle (present only for existing accounts).

buildProrationBreakdown echoes full internal error details to the client whenever the caller passes reportLevel=itemized: return reply.code(500).send({ error: err.message, stack: err.stack, buildingId, totalAmount }). This leaks stack traces, file paths, and internal logic to any staff user (information disclosure).

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: postAutopayCharge embeds a live ledger partner bearer token as a hardcoded string literal ('lgr_7f0c...') in source, whereas postManualSettlement correctly reads LEDGER_PARTNER_TOKEN from the environment. The hardcoded secret is exposed to anyone with repo access and cannot be rotated independently.

sendOverdueSmsViaLegacyGateway sends the carrier API key as a query-string parameter over plaintext HTTP (http://sms-gateway.internal-carrier.example/send?api_key=...). The credential is exposed in transit and in proxy/access logs; the current gateway integration (sendTicketSmsViaGateway) correctly uses a Bearer header over HTTPS.

issueDeviceTrustCookie sets a long-lived device-trust credential cookie (Max-Age 30 days) without HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite attributes (issueHardenedDeviceTrustCookie is the safe twin that adds HttpOnly; SameSite=Strict; Secure in production). The token is therefore readable by page JavaScript (XSS-theft) and transmitted over cleartext connections.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: escalateTicketPriority writes the user-supplied reason directly into the ops activity log line: req.log.info(`ticket ${id} escalated ...: ${reason}`). A crafted reason containing newlines can inject forged log entries (log injection / log spoofing). escalateTicketPriorityReviewed is the safe twin that strips [\r\n\0] from reason first.

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: enrollLeaseAutopay stores the tenant's full bank account number and routing number in plaintext columns on the leases table (lease.autopayBankAccount / autopayRoutingNumber) without encryption or masking, unlike the field-level AES-GCM used for screening SSNs elsewhere. Sensitive financial data at rest (CWE-312).

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
